source.title: SAE Training Dataset Influence in Feature Matching and a Hypothesis on Position Features

record.tranche_reason: The study measures SAE feature matching across training settings and reports that feature identity varies, especially with dataset and dictionary size. This refines the claim that SAE features are stable, canonical units.
record.gate_note: The study tests decoder-weight feature matching across training settings, which bears on V5. Its activation visualizations and positional-encoding ablations concern position-related activation patterns, not the listed versions about superposition or SAE feature recovery. Table 1 matching ratios and Table 2 feature-count differences are included; qualitative Figure 11 descriptions repeat those comparisons. Cross-dataset reconstruction metrics in the comments do not directly measure feature identity.
record.test_reason: The study trains 73 GPT2-small layer-8 SAEs and measures how far decoder-weight features match across dataset, seed, dictionary size, architecture and sparsity. Those results bear directly on whether SAE features are stable, canonical units (V5), and they show substantial variation.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The author concludes that dataset influences the SAE feature set more than seed, with sparsity and architecture mattering less, and that dictionary size changes abstraction level. Additions: seed matching fell with larger dictionaries, refuting the author's convergence hypothesis. The author also hypothesizes a position-feature set in early layers. Matching without the Hungarian algorithm may overestimate similarity.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses decoder-weight cosine similarity and a threshold to compare SAE dictionaries across GPT2-small training settings, rather than the original toy-model procedure. It also compares encoder- and neuron-weight matching methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Feature matching varied with dataset, seed, dictionary size, SAE architecture, and sparsity setting. The authors report dataset as the strongest influence.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE feature-activation averages oscillate with token position, at a doubled frequency in layers 1–3. The pattern vanishes when positional embeddings are ablated or shuffled.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Early-layer SAE features include a distinct position-feature set tied to GPT-2's helical positional embedding.

fits_no_version.finding: Early layers show lower adjacent-layer feature matching than later layers (Figure 13).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-layer SAE feature persistence increases with depth.

record.problems: Only GPT2-small was studied. Matching uses a thresholded cosine-based method rather than one-to-one Hungarian matching, which the authors say may overestimate similarity and makes comparison with prior results less strict. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the matching ratios.
record.rows_left_out: Left out qualitative Figure 11 matching descriptions because they repeat the comparisons summarized in Table 1. Left out Figure 13 cross-layer matching and feature-activation/positional-encoding results because they do not directly test whether SAE features are complete, stable canonical units. Left out the comments' cross-dataset reconstruction metrics because they measure reconstruction quality rather than feature identity.

untested.parts: All of it: no toy models, sparsity transition or geometry.
All of it: no test of capacity competition.
Whether real-model features are spread across neurons. SAEs are used but recovery of true sparse features is not tested.
Completeness of SAE features and interpretability of the matched versus unmatched features. Only decoder-direction overlap on one model and one layer was measured.
All of it: the dimensionality of features is not tested.

missing.what: Matching ratio between checkpoints of the same SAE at 1e8 vs 4e8 training tokens (~0.7). This shows feature identity still shifts during training.
Cross-dataset reconstruction: explained variance stays near 1 across web datasets despite low feature matching, but CE and L2 loss are 2–3x higher off-dataset. TinyStories SAEs generalize poorly.
Encoder-based and decoder-based matching give considerably different matching ratios. The stability result therefore depends on which weights are compared.

record.verdict_notes: The record's 'challenges' label for the dataset rows is replaced with limits_scope. The rows show low but nonzero overlap, and with no null baseline they are not absent or reversed. N1–N6 are unlinked as threshold-justification values. The study covers a single model (GPT2-small), mainly layer 8, and reports no uncertainty.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model storage geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity or allocates dedicated dimensions to important features.
Whether polysemanticity can arise for reasons other than capacity pressure.
The study does not establish that real-model features are spread across neurons or that SAE features recover underlying sparse features.

Matching is based on decoder-weight cosine similarity with a threshold, not a demonstration that features are complete or canonical; the study does not establish feature stability under all models or settings.
The study compares feature-direction vectors but does not test whether underlying features are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.
